title: Counting bound for bad restrictions of a DNF
statement:
Let $f$ be a DNF formula on $n$ Boolean variables in which no two literals of the same term share a variable and no term lists the same literal twice, and suppose every term of $f$ has at most $w$ literals. Fix natural numbers $d \le s$. Then the number of restrictions of the $n$ variables that leave exactly $s$ variables free and are bad for $f$ at depth $d$ — that is, for which the restricted function $x \mapsto f(\rho.\mathrm{extend}\,x)$ has decision-tree depth strictly greater than $d$ — is at most
\[
\binom{n}{\,s-d\,}\, 2^{\,n-(s-d)}\, (4w)^{d}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: every term of f has at most w literals (DNF width ≤ w)
within each term, two literals with the same variable are equal
each term has no duplicate literals
ρ leaves exactly s variables free
ρ is bad for f at depth d (restricted function has decision-tree depth > d)
replaced:
For $d \leq s$, the number of bad $s$-restrictions is at most
$\binom{n}{s-d}\,2^{\,n-(s-d)}\,(4w)^d$: every bad $s$-restriction is mapped by
$\mathrm{razborovEncode}$ to a $\gamma$ with exactly $s-d$ free variables, each
fiber of this map has size at most $(4w)^d$, and there are
$\binom{n}{s-d}\,2^{\,n-(s-d)}$ possible values of $\gamma$.
